source: (Ahab standing by the helm. Starbuck approaching him.)
“We must send down the main-top-sail yard, sir. The band is working loose and the lee lift is half-stranded. Shall I strike it, sir?”
“Strike nothing; lash it. If I had sky-sail poles, I’d sway them up now.”
“The anchors are working, sir. Shall I get them inboard?”

“Strike nothing, and stir nothing, but lash everything. The wind rises, but it has not got up to my table-lands yet. Quick, and see to it.—By masts and keels! he takes me for the hunch-backed skipper of some coasting smack. Send down my main-top-sail yard! Ho, gluepots! Loftiest trucks were made for wildest winds, and this brain-truck of mine now sails amid the cloud-scud. Shall I strike that? Oh, none but cowards send down their brain-trucks in tempest time. What a hooroosh aloft there! I would e’en take it for sublime, did I not know that the colic is a noisy malady. Oh, take medicine, take medicine!”

modern_en.title: Chapter 120 — The Deck Towards the End of the First Night Watch
paragraphs: Ahab standing by the helm. Starbuck approaching him.
"We have to send down the main-topsail yard, sir. The band is working loose, and half the strands of the lee lift have parted. Should I strike it, sir?"
"Strike nothing; lash it. If I had sky-sail poles, I'd sway them up now."
"Sir! — in God's name! — sir?"
"Well."
"The anchors are working, sir. Shall I get them inboard?"

"Strike nothing and stir nothing, but lash everything down. The wind is rising, but it hasn't reached my tablelands yet. Quick, see to it. — By masts and keels! He takes me for the hunchbacked skipper of some little coasting smack. Send down my main-topsail yard! Ho, you gluepots! The loftiest trucks were made for the wildest winds, and this brain-truck of mine is sailing now among the scudding clouds. Should I strike that? Oh, only cowards send down their brain-trucks in a storm. What a hullabaloo up there! I'd almost take it for the sublime, if I didn't know that colic is a noisy illness. Oh, take some medicine, take some medicine!"

modern_da.title: Kapitel 120 — Dækket mod slutningen af den første nattevagt
paragraphs: Ahab står ved rorpinden. Starbuck nærmer sig ham.
»Vi må sende store mærsrå ned, sir. Båndet er ved at give sig, og halvdelen af tampene på læ-lifteren er sprunget. Skal jeg stryge den, sir?«
»Stryg intet. Surr den fast. Havde jeg rundholter til skysejl, ville jeg hejse dem op nu.«
»Sir! — I Guds navn! — sir?«
»Nå.«
»Ankrene arbejder, sir. Skal jeg få dem indenbords?«

»Stryg intet og rør intet, men surr alt fast. Vinden er ved at tage til, men den har ikke nået mine højsletter endnu. Hurtigt, sørg for det. — Ved master og kølstokke! Han tager mig for den pukkelryggede skipper på en lille kystsmakke. Send min store mærsrå ned! Hov, I limpotter! De højeste mastetoppe blev lavet til de vildeste vinde, og denne mastetop af en hjerne sejler nu blandt de jagende skyer. Skulle jeg stryge den? Åh, kun kujoner sender deres hjernetoppe ned i en storm. Sikke et ramaskrig deroppe! Jeg ville næsten tage det for det ophøjede, hvis jeg ikke vidste, at kolik er en støjende sygdom. Åh, tag noget medicin, tag noget medicin!«
